  • Federal opportunity identification and qualification across SAM.gov, GSA Schedules, agency forecasts, and prime/sub channels
  • Capture-to-proposal lifecycle: opportunity assessment, teaming strategy, technical and price strategy, color-team reviews, submission readiness
  • Capture playbook documentation: pursuit criteria, gate reviews, win themes, ghosting strategy, competitive analysis
  • Prime and sub partner relationships and government POC management
  • Set-aside strategy and certification work (8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, SDVOSB) in coordination with the GovCon Division Lead
  • Pipeline visibility and reporting to firm leadership
  • Coaching the Proposal Manager and Federal Account Executive seats as they come online

Engagement structure

Hourly consulting rate, three tiers calibrated to experience and scope:

  • Foundational ($100-200/hr): Capture managers with 5-8 years experience, ramping into a director role
  • Director ($200-350/hr): Established capture directors with documented win history on $1M+ contracts
  • Principal ($350-500/hr): Senior capture principals with multi-million-dollar award history and Tier 1 prime experience

Engagement is hourly. Time commitment scales with pipeline activity, typically 10-40 hours per week. Win-based bonus stack negotiable on top of hourly rate for awarded contracts the engagement materially drove.

Success milestones

  • Day 30: Capture playbook drafted. Pursuit gate criteria documented. Initial pipeline of 10+ qualified opportunities.
  • Day 90: 2-4 active captures in formal pursuit. First teaming agreements signed. Pipeline value $1M+.
  • Day 180: 2-4 proposals submitted. First award or shortlist position. Win rate baseline established.

Who you are

  • 7-15 years in federal capture, proposal management, or BD for small to mid-size GovCon firms
  • Documented track record capturing $1M+ federal contracts
  • Shipley-trained or equivalent. SAM.gov fluent. Comfortable with FAR/DFARS terminology
  • Familiar with small business set-asides and the certification lifecycle
  • Past performance citations in workforce, HHS-adjacent, hospitality, or staffing services preferred
  • Comfortable building a function from scratch inside a founder-led firm
  • Located in DC, NC, GA, or willing to travel to DC quarterly

Bonus points

  • Prior role at a Tier 1 GovCon prime or boutique capture firm
  • Existing relationships at DoD, VA, HHS, GSA, or DHS
  • APMP credential
  • Track record of managed HUBZone or 8(a) certifications

How we will get to know each other

  1. Initial 30-minute fit conversation with the GovCon Division Lead
  2. Working session: walk through a real federal opportunity or proposal scenario we are actively considering
  3. Reference checks (3+ professional references) and work history verification
  4. Engagement letter, scope of work, and rate confirmation
  5. Kickoff within 7 days of signed engagement

2-4 weeks first conversation to active engagement.

What we believe

Trust before revenue. Mission before money. Real seats, real upside. We build durable federal relationships through earned credibility. We win together. We pay people in real numbers, not pizza parties. We are building something great and we want partners who feel the same.

Application tips

  1. Visit , ,
  2. Find The Wilkinson Firm on LinkedIn
  3. In your cover note, answer two questions: (1) what kind of GovCon engagement model works best for you (project-based, retained hours, hybrid), and (2) one example of a federal pursuit, proposal, or account you would point to as your strongest reference work

What to expect from us

  • Reply within 48 hours
  • First-round conversation within 7 days of qualification
  • Full process: 2-4 weeks
  • We tell you yes or no. We do not ghost.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff to the Founder and CEO
jobs.excerpt: Where this is goingWe are a founder-led group of B2B software companies serving the private wealth and governance world: WealthComply (FATCA and CRS compliance automation), MinuteMaster (board minutes and governance automation), a venture that is in stealth, and a small media strategy company.
jobs.description:
Where this is going

We are a founder-led group of B2B software companies serving the private wealth and governance world: WealthComply (FATCA and CRS compliance automation), MinuteMaster (board minutes and governance automation), a venture that is in stealth, and a small media strategy company. The founder is based in Jersey. The team works from several countries. Our clients are trust companies, fund administrators and private wealth firms across Europe, the Middle East, Asia and the Caribbean.

Over the next three years we want a group with a real leadership team, where the founder spends his time on the few things only a founder can do and everything else runs without him. This role makes that happen. If that pulls you, read on. If it does not, this is a good place to stop.


The role

You run the founder's office across the group. You work through other people, with authority the founder lends you openly. In practice:

  • You own the operating rhythm: the daily check-in, the weekly business review, the Friday update, the decision log.
  • You take the workstreams that have no natural owner (a funding round's mechanics, an alliance agreement, a pricing clean-up, a specialist pool) from a conversation to a one-page recommendation, then you execute what the founder decides.
  • You curate what reaches him. Every decision arrives as one page: the decision, the options, a recommendation, a deadline.
  • You close the loops that need a person: chasing, calls, counsel, the company secretary, candidates.
  • You run hiring with our recruiter (scorecards, interviews, references, trials, onboarding) so the founder interviews and decides, and does nothing else in the process.
  • You take on the group's operating admin (payroll, banking within limits, tools, the filing calendar) until it is documented and handed to the right owner. The aim is to remove it, then move on.
  • You will be in the room with the co-founders, investors' teams and advisers. When the team needs a decision or an owner, you are the person they come to.
  • The office runs on an AI operating layer we have already built and use daily: the record, the cadence documents, meeting prep, first drafts. You direct it, and you are accountable for what it produces. If Claude or something like it is already how you work, you will feel at home.


You will be judged on five things

  1. The founder's hours coming back to the work only he can do. We measure it.
  2. Every decision that reaches him arriving as one page.
  3. The rhythm running when he is away or tired.
  4. Two senior hires landed through our process in your first six months.
  5. Nothing falling through: filings, payments, commitments, follow-ups.


This role will not suit you if

  • You want a team under you and a budget of your own. You work through others here.
  • You are an excellent executive assistant looking for the next title. This role decides inside its own authority and answers for the outcome.
  • You produce analysis and decks and leave the doing to others. Every workstream here ends in something that happened.
  • You need the founder in every loop. The job exists to take him out of most of them.
  • You do not already use AI in your daily work.
  • You want a guaranteed bonus, or you find it hard to be corrected.


Who you are

  • An exceptional writer. You can turn a messy forty-minute conversation into a one-page memo with an honest recommendation. We test this before we meet you.
  • You close loops across people who do not report to you, and you can name the last three.
  • You are comfortable around senior people. You can carry the founder's proxy with two experienced co-founders on follow-through, without grabbing or shrinking.
  • You are numerate and discreet. You will see cap tables, salaries and co-founder terms, and handle payroll and banking within limits.
  • AI is already how you research, draft, analyse and automate. You know what you are asking for before you ask, and you check what comes back.
  • Humble, hungry, happy. You would rather be corrected than be right. You find the binding constraint and work on it. People are glad when you join the call.
  • You work at a pace you can keep. We want someone who is still great in year three.


What we offer

  • Equity, so you share in the value created after you join. If we hit our plan it is worth many times your base. If we miss it, it is worth nothing. We would rather you did that maths than have us do it for you.
  • An outcomes bonus, paid on results.
  • Remote on UK hours, with a week in Jersey each month for the first quarter while trust and context build, then quarterly, plus one proper offsite a year.
  • Home office, learning and wellbeing budgets, and the AI tool stack paid for.
  • Rest as a design constraint. We work at a pace we can keep, and after the annual reporting crunch we slow down on purpose.
  • A written path: chief of staff for two to three years, then head of operations for the group or a line you helped create.


How we hire

Our recruiter runs the process. It includes a short paid writing exercise, a paid working session on real anonymised tasks so we see how you actually work, conversations with the founder and a co-founder, references (including, with your permission, one we choose), and a paid trial. We move as fast as the right person allows, and we tell you where you stand after every step. The offer comes with a sixty-day review against outcomes we agree together. We say that now because we mean it both ways.


How to apply

Apply through the link. Along with your CV or LinkedIn profile, we ask three short questions: something you built, started or fixed that nobody asked for and that cost you something (up to 300 words); which of the "who you are" points you are weakest on (one line); and your location and salary expectation. No cover letter. If you are not sure you tick every box, apply anyway.

About you:

To thrive in ArborBridge’s Online SAT/ACT Tutor position, it’s helpful if you are…

An Engaging and Effective Educator.

Education is your passion, and private, one-on-one online tutoring is your ideal method for providing a top-notch experience for your students and their families. You’re not interested in on-demand homework help. Instead, you are an expert at creating a personalized tutoring program: You map out customized lesson plans, solidify practice test timelines, identify the right amount of homework, and propose the ideal meeting schedule to help your students reach their goals. You understand that building relationships with your students and their families is a key part of the process, and you can adapt to various needs with ease.

A Quick and Thorough Communicator.

You also understand that part of building relationships is being a reliable and clear communicator. You make it a priority to respond to phone calls and emails from parents, students, and your ArborBridge colleagues in a quick and thorough manner. You know that excellent communication = excellent customer service, and you strive to provide the very best.

An Organized and Proactive Problem-Solver.

You remember well how stressful the test-taking process can be, and you are always thinking of ways you can ease the burden for your clients. You’re adept at spotting potential problems in a program from a mile away and proactive about addressing them as soon as possible. If you get a message from a concerned parent or a colleague who needs your input on a program, you are quick to respond and prepared to offer multiple solutions.

What you’ve accomplished:

  • At least 6 months of formal tutoring experience (1 year or more is preferred).
  • Comfort tutoring all sections of the SAT & ACT.
  • Familiarity with online teaching tools.
  • Bachelor’s degree from a top university.

How your skills and passion come to life at ArborBridge:

  • Privately tutoring students around the world via Zoom, an online video conferencing platform
  • Creating personalized test prep plans for each student
  • Setting consistent instructional and practice exam schedules for each student, with the goal of making steady progress leading up to a specific test date
  • Writing lesson summaries after each meeting with a student, updating parents on the student’s progress
  • Assigning appropriate amounts of homework between lessons
  • Establishing genuine relationships with your students, their families, and ArborBridge employees
  • Communicating regularly with program managers, instruction managers, directors of tutoring, operational staff, and other colleagues at ArborBridge to ensure that students receive maximum support and each program runs smoothly

Compensation and benefits:

  • $35 per hour for instructional time, with opportunities for annual performance-based raises
  • $11 per hour or your local minimum wage, if higher, for administrative time (automatically added to paycheck at a rate of 20 minutes per instructional hour)
  • No noncompete clause—you can work for other tutoring companies when you work for ArborBridge
  • Work from home
  • Flexible hours
  • Professional development
  • Opportunities for growth

This position requires approximately 18 hours of self-directed and manager-led training time, which is paid at our training rate of $15/hour.

About ArborBridge:

ArborBridge is a premier test preparation company and tutoring firm, delivering one-on-one tutoring to students in more than 50 countries around the world. We specialize in SAT and ACT preparation and offer extensive tutoring for AP exams, ISEE and SSAT, graduate exams, and academic subjects. With the most sophisticated diagnostic algorithm in the industry and more individual lesson plans than any other company, ArborBridge is the most highly customized and efficient platform on the market. Our elite tutors meet with students online and in-person and build programs around individual needs, making the most of time and maximizing learning.

ArborBridge is committed to developing an inclusive work environment in which a flourishing, diverse team celebrates the contributions of individuals.

jobs.description:
As a Senior Partner Solutions Engineer at vCluster Labs, you aren’t just supporting partner deals; you are building the technical foundation of our partner ecosystem from the ground up. You will be our first dedicated partner-facing pre-sales engineer, turning relationships with NVIDIA, WWT, AMD, and AI Cloud providers like Nebius into validated reference architectures, enabled partner architects, and partner-sourced pipeline. Where there’s a GPU, vCluster needs to be there, and you are the person who makes that real: someone who can whiteboard a GPU cloud architecture with an NVIDIA solution architect in the morning and train a room of partner sellers in the afternoon.

As a Senior Partner Solutions Engineer, your role will include:

  • Joint Reference Architectures: Design and validate reference architectures with strategic partners, from NVIDIA blueprints and AMD foundations up through the platform layer: vCluster, vNode, vMetal, and vCluster Platform. Turn one successful deployment into a repeatable, sellable solution with bills of material, deployment guides, demo environments, and benchmarks.

  • Partner Enablement: Build and deliver technical enablement for partner architects and sellers, including training dozens of architects at partner Centers of Excellence on the value proposition, cost, and performance story of the vCluster product family, so partners position us to win when we are not in the room.

  • Field Enablement: Enable vCluster’s internal field SEs to engage partners effectively, so the partner motion scales beyond one person and the field is never pulled off customers to cover channel work.

  • Partner-Led Opportunities: Own technical discovery, demos, and Proofs of Concept for partner-sourced opportunities, always in support of direct field ownership. Run a disciplined POC model: validated business problem, named sponsor, clear success criteria, and a defined production milestone.

  • Centers of Excellence: Stand up vCluster presence inside partner Centers of Excellence, such as WWT’s in St. Louis, tied to named customers and qualified pipeline rather than marketing labs.

  • Ecosystem Navigation: Build technical credibility across a focused set of 6–8 priority partners, cultivating executive sponsors and technical champions without becoming dependent on a single contact or business unit.

This role could be a fit for you if you bring:

  • Deep Kubernetes expertise: You go deep on cluster architecture, Tenant Isolation, and the cloud-native ecosystem, and you can master vCluster, vNode, and vMetal inside and out. This one is required, not preferred.

  • Partner pre-sales experience: You have worked with partners (OEMs, GSIs, resellers, or cloud providers) in a technical pre-sales capacity and you understand the partner dynamic: co-selling, joint validation, and winning through someone else’s sellers.

  • Solutions engineering craft: Years of discovery, whiteboarding, demos, and POCs that actually convert to production, with the qualification discipline to say no to science projects.

  • Enablement building: You have created enablement content, workshops, hands-on labs, or certification paths from scratch, and the partners you enabled kept winning after you left the room.

  • Executive presence: You can hold the room with a Kubernetes engineer and a CIO in the same meeting, and you move people you don’t manage.

Bonus points for:

  • NVIDIA ecosystem experience: DGX, Dynamo, GPU Operator, AI Enterprise, or NVIDIA certifications, plus an understanding of how NVIDIA blueprints and partner validation actually work.

  • AI infrastructure depth: GPU infrastructure, storage, and networking for AI factories and GPU clouds (Weka- and VAST-class storage literacy is a plus).

  • AI Cloud or GPU-as-a-Service experience: Time building or supporting GPU-as-a-Service or Kubernetes-as-a-Service platforms at AI Cloud providers or service providers.

About vCluster Labs

We're the #1 platform for AI infrastructure, trusted by the world's fastest-growing AI cloud builders. We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.

We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.

We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. At KubeCon North America 2025, we launched our Infrastructure Tenancy Platform for AI, a Kubernetes-native framework built for running AI, ML, and GPU-intensive workloads anywhere, with an NVIDIA-validated reference architecture for DGX systems.

Benefits

We offer the following benefits:

  • Competitive Salary: We offer a competitive compensation package, including equity.

  • Premium Insurance: Health, dental, vision, and life Insurance, including plans for you and eligible dependents (benefits vary depending on country).

  • Flexible Working Schedule: You have a doctor’s appointment or need to head to the supermarket to get groceries at 2pm? We won’t have an issue with that. To us, results matter more than clocking in and out at the same time every day.

  • Workplace Flexibility: We’re very flexible about where you work. We know things can change in life and we’re happy to adjust the work environment for you along the way.

Culture & Values

At vCluster Labs, we value and stand for:

  1. Make it Happen: We have a relentless bias for action and the grit to push through obstacles. We do whatever it takes to figure it out, put in the work, and ruthlessly prioritize the actions that drive measurable impact for the business.

  2. Own the Outcome: We understand that our responsibility doesn't end when a task is checked off; it ends when the value is delivered. We connect our daily individual actions to the broader success of the company and our customers.

  3. Create Wow: We measure success by the experience we generate, both inside and outside the company. For our customers, this means impressive speed and intuitive experiences. For our team, this means going the extra mile to support one another and to continuously drive each other to new heights.

  4. Open Source, Open Mind: We are actively contributing to and maintaining open-source projects. Internally, we foster meritocracy — the strongest ideas win, no matter who or where they come from.

  5. Build Tomorrow’s Standards, Intentionally: We don't just ship software; we define the state-of-the-art of tomorrow. We are fearless in tearing down old approaches to build something better, but we are disciplined in how we do it because we know our users rely on our technology to run mission-critical infrastructure platforms.

jobs.description:
About Abridge

Abridge was founded in 2018 with the mission of powering deeper understanding in healthcare. Our AI-powered platform was purpose-built for medical conversations, improving clinical documentation efficiencies while enabling clinicians to focus on what matters most—their patients.

Our enterprise-grade technology transforms patient-clinician conversations into structured clinical notes in real-time, with deep EMR integrations. Powered by Linked Evidence and our purpose-built, auditable AI, we are the only company that maps AI-generated summaries to ground truth, helping providers quickly trust and verify the output. As pioneers in generative AI for healthcare, we are setting the industry standards for the responsible deployment of AI across health systems.

We are a growing team of practicing MDs, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to empower people and make care make more sense. We have offices located in the Mission District in San Francisco, the SoHo neighborhood of New York, and East Liberty in Pittsburgh.

The Role

Abridge is growing rapidly and we're building out the Product Operations and Strategy team to help our product organization scale with excellence. Your time will be split between execution (fixing systems that no longer scale, running cross-functional workstreams end-to-end, keeping the team shipping with speed) and forward-looking strategy (helping product leadership see around corners, forming a point of view on what new bets we should be pursuing). You will flex across both, and the exact split will shift by quarter as the team's needs change. Day-to-day, you’ll be embedded within our Builders org and act as a key operating partner to product leadership, while working closely with cross-functional partners across Partner Experience, Commercial, and Finance.

Reporting into the Senior Manager of Product Operations & Strategy, this is a hands-on, high-impact role for a high-EQ, structured thinker with GSD energy who loves building the operating system of a world-class product org.

This is a hybrid role with a minimum of 3 days weekly in our San Francisco office. Please only apply if you are able to commit to this model and/or willing to relocate to San Francisco.

What You'll Do

Below is a representative sample of current priorities. Expect them to shift quarter to quarter as the team scales.

Execution and process design

  • Identify product development processes that no longer scale and ship better ones in days.

  • Get PMs and builders in front of customers, and close the loop between field signal and roadmap decisions.

  • Design systems that surface key product knowledge and roadmap visibility throughout the org, so we continue to stay in sync as we scale.

  • Reinvent how we hire and cultivate product talent, from redesigning our interview process to sharpening onboarding so new hires ramp to creating user value faster.

Strategy and forward planning

  • Ramp on the thorniest strategic questions product leadership needs answered, drive them to clear recommendations, and implement end-to-end.

  • Translate shifts in the competitive landscape and regulatory environment into roadmap and GTM implications.

  • Develop points of view on new bets and adjacent markets the company should be running at next.

Builder velocity and AI enablement

  • Shape and measure the program that holds engineering and product teams accountable for real AI adoption. Treat every new AI tool as a chance to compound builder velocity.

  • Host clinician and builder hackathons that strengthen our connection to the broader builder and clinician community.

  • Build a shared context layer for the product org that powers our AI tooling and learns in real time, surfacing field insight and customer signal to the people who need it.

What You'll Bring

  • 2+ years in consulting, investment banking, investing or similar roles (startup experience on top of that is a plus)

  • Incredibly AI-pilled. This is a requirement of the role. You use AI tools every day, at work and on the side. You try new tools the week they launch and you build systems yourself (scripts, agents, workflows)

  • Bias to action. High ownership mentality. You would rather ship something imperfect and iterate than over-plan.

  • High EQ and the ability to influence without authority. You earn trust from engineers, PMs, GTM leaders, and executives because you are clear, reliable, and useful.

  • First-principles thinker. You design operating systems that fit the context you're in, not playbooks copied from somewhere else.

  • Numerate. You can present a point of view backed by analysis. You are as comfortable in a spreadsheet as in a stakeholder meeting.

  • Comfort with ambiguity. The mix of execution and strategy will shift quarter by quarter. You are energized by that, not destabilized.

Why Work at Abridge?

At Abridge, we’re transforming healthcare delivery experiences with generative AI, enabling clinicians and patients to connect in deeper, more meaningful ways. Our mission is clear: to power deeper understanding in healthcare. We’re driving real, lasting change, with millions of medical conversations processed each month.

Joining Abridge means stepping into a fast-paced, high-growth startup where your contributions truly make a difference. Our culture requires extreme ownership—every employee has the ability to (and is expected to) make an impact on our customers and our business.

Beyond individual impact, you will have the opportunity to work alongside a team of curious, high-achieving people in a supportive environment where success is shared, growth is constant, and feedback fuels progress. At Abridge, it’s not just what we do—it’s how we do it. Every decision is rooted in empathy, always prioritizing the needs of clinicians and patients.

We’re committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally. Whether it's flexible work hours, an inclusive culture, or ongoing learning opportunities, we are here to help you thrive and do the best work of your life.

If you are ready to make a meaningful impact alongside passionate people who care deeply about what they do, Abridge is the place for you.

How we take care of Abridgers:

  • Generous Time Off: 14 paid holidays, flexible PTO for salaried employees, and accrued time off for hourly employees

  • Comprehensive Health Plans: Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage for all full-time employees and their families.

  • Generous HSA Contribution: If you choose a High Deductible Health Plan, Abridge makes monthly contributions to your HSA.

  • Paid Parental Leave: Generous paid parental leave for all full-time employees.

  • Family Forming Benefits: Resources and financial support to help you build your family.

  • 401(k) Matching: Contribution matching to help invest in your future.

  • Personal Device Allowance: Tax free funds for personal device usage.

  • Pre-tax Benefits: Access to Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) and Commuter Benefits.

  • Lifestyle Wallet: Monthly contributions for fitness, professional development, coworking, and more.

  • Mental Health Support: Dedicated access to therapy and coaching to help you reach your goals.

  • Sabbatical Leave: Paid Sabbatical Leave after 5 years of employment.

  • Compensation and Equity: Competitive compensation and equity grants for full time employees.

  • ... and much more!

Equal Opportunity Employer

Abridge is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants equally without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or disability.

We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the interview process. Once you submit your application, we'll follow up with details on how to request an accommodation for interviewing, completing any assessments, or otherwise participating in the selection process.

Staying safe - Protect yourself from recruitment fraud

We are aware of individuals and entities fraudulently representing themselves as Abridge recruiters and/or hiring managers. Abridge will never ask for financial information or payment, or for personal information such as bank account number or social security number during the job application or interview process. Any emails from the Abridge recruiting team will come from an @abridge.com email address. You can learn more about how to protect yourself from these types of fraud by referring to this article. Please exercise caution and cease communications if something feels suspicious about your interactions.

The ideal candidate combines marketplace or ecommerce expertise with strong analytical judgment, commercial instincts, and the ability to operate at both strategic and hands-on levels. This position reports to the General Manager of Marketplace.

What you will be doing

Lead marketplace performance and inventory analytics

  • Own the measurement framework for Marketplace commerce performance, from member engagement and conversion through transaction completion, revenue, retention, and lifetime value.
  • Evaluate the performance of our inventory across merchants, products, categories, offer types, and member segments.
  • Monitor key marketplace economics, including transaction volume, revenue, take rate, margin, merchant performance, and offer quality.
  • Identify underperforming inventory, emerging member needs, assortment gaps, and opportunities to improve product and category mix.
  • Develop dashboards, reporting, and executive-level insights that explain not only what happened, but why it happened and what the business should do next.
  • Establish consistent metric definitions and reconcile internal data with affiliate network, merchant, and vendor reporting.
  • Identify and close measurement gaps, such as bridging HealthEquity platform metrics with affiliate or brand metrics to evaluate funnel performance or attribution.

Build subscription and retention intelligence

  • Own analytics for subscription and recurring-revenue products as a distinct business model within the Marketplace portfolio.
  • Develop acquisition, activation, retention, churn, renewal, and lifetime-value reporting by product, cohort, channel, offer, and member segment.
  • Diagnose the drivers of subscription churn and retention, distinguishing acquisition-quality issues from product, pricing, engagement, and lifecycle factors.
  • Partner with Product, Growth, and merchant teams to identify retention opportunities and prioritize interventions.
  • Design measurement approaches for onboarding improvements, lifecycle communications, pricing changes, save offers, and other retention initiatives.

Optimize offers, pricing, and promotions

  • Build a fact base for competitive offers, including offer structure, discount depth, funding model, cadence, eligibility, and market positioning.
  • Advise Growth, Marketing, Product, and merchant teams on offer and promotion design before launch.
  • Measure the incremental impact of offers and promotions, separating true lift from demand that would have occurred without the incentive.
  • Evaluate tradeoffs among conversion, member value, merchant funding, Marketplace economics, and long-term customer behavior.
  • Establish testing and measurement standards for promotions, including experiments, holdouts, matched comparisons, and other causal-inference methods where appropriate.
  • Translate findings into practical recommendations about which offers to scale, modify, or discontinue.

Advance segmentation and targeting

  • Partner with Data Science and Engineering to define member segments and develop propensity and affinity scores by category, product, and offer type.
  • Translate commercial questions into clear data and model requirements, success criteria, and activation plans.
  • Help Product and Marketing apply segmentation across onsite and offsite experiences to improve relevance and conversion.
  • Monitor model and targeting performance to ensure recommendations produce measurable business value.

What you will need to be successful

  • 7+ years of experience in analytics, decision science, business intelligence, or a related discipline, including experience supporting a marketplace, ecommerce, subscription, affiliate marketing, or similar business.
  • Strong understanding of marketplace or ecommerce economics, including conversion, revenue, margin, take rate, and promotional efficiency.
  • Experience analyzing subscription funnels, retention cohorts, churn, and customer lifetime value.
  • Practical expertise in experimentation, incrementality measurement, attribution, and causal analysis.
  • Strong judgment and intellectual curiosity

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with card-funded or card-linked offers, including merchant funding, attribution, redemption, and unit economics.

Engagement type: Independent consultant, 1099 hourly.
Rate range: $100 - $500 per hour, based on experience and scope (three-tier band detailed below).
Time commitment: Part-time or fractional, scales with account activity.
Location: Remote, with DC and agency travel as opportunities require.
Reports to: GovCon Division Lead.

A note from the founder

Federal sales is a long game built on the credibility of every conversation. The Federal Account Executive is the operator who carries our name into agency offices, prime contractor partnerships, and small business outreach events. Equal parts hunter and contracts literate. The seat is built for someone who wants to be paid for the relationships they own and the doors they open.

What is already built

The Wilkinson Firm is a workforce strategy and staffing firm headquartered across NC and Atlanta. Year 2 of operations. Two operational divisions today (HR Advisory for the mental health industry, Premium Hospitality and Event Staffing). Government Contracting division being formally stood up this quarter. Three active staffing contracts in delivery. FY26 trajectory $425-525K. Zero loans, zero institutional debt.

Bench credentials: Former EEOC Administrative Law Judge, employment attorneys, clinical advisors, 32-year enterprise operations specialist.

What you own

  • Federal customer targeting across our priority verticals (HHS workforce, VA behavioral health, DoD behavioral health support, federal hospitality)
  • Account development: agency POC outreach, small business office relationships, prime contractor BD relationships, industry day attendance
  • Pipeline development feeding the Federal Capture Director with qualified opportunities
  • Federal contracts literacy: FAR/DFARS basics, SAM.gov management, set-aside qualification (8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, SDVOSB), small business certification lifecycle
  • Capability statement positioning and customer-tailored briefings
  • HubSpot CRM hygiene for the GovCon pipeline
  • Cross-coordination with the Capture Director on captured opportunities and the Proposal Manager on past performance inputs

Engagement structure

Hourly consulting rate, three tiers calibrated to experience and scope:

  • Foundational ($100-200/hr): Federal sales operators with 3-7 years agency or prime contractor BD experience
  • Senior ($200-350/hr): Established federal AEs with documented relationships at named agencies
  • Principal ($350-500/hr): Senior federal account principals with multi-agency portfolios and existing prime relationships

Engagement is hourly. Time commitment scales with active account development, typically 10-30 hours per week. Win-based bonus stack negotiable on top of hourly rate for awarded contracts where the engagement materially sourced the relationship.

Success milestones

  • Day 30: Target account list documented and approved. Capability statement positioning sharpened. Initial outreach cadence active.
  • Day 90: 10+ qualified agency or prime contractor conversations logged. 3+ teaming or partnership discussions advancing. Pipeline visibility documented in HubSpot.
  • Day 180: 2-4 captured opportunities handed off to the Capture Director. First responded RFP or RFI. First named agency relationship producing visible activity.

Who you are

  • 5-12 years in federal sales, agency BD, prime contractor account management, or government affairs
  • Documented relationships at one or more of: DoD (behavioral health, lodging, F&B), VA (mental health programs, workforce), HHS (workforce IDIQs), GSA, DHS
  • Working fluency in FAR/DFARS basics, set-aside qualification, and federal procurement vocabulary
  • Comfortable with SAM.gov, GSA Schedules, and small business certification mechanics
  • Strong outbound voice and the ability to convert cold outreach into recurring meetings
  • Comfortable working inside a founder-led firm building its federal motion from the ground up
  • Located in DC, NC, GA, or willing to travel to DC quarterly

Bonus points

  • Prior role at a Tier 1 GovCon prime, boutique federal sales shop, or agency BD team
  • Past role inside DoD, VA, HHS, GSA, or DHS as a contracting officer, technical representative, or program staff
  • APMP credential
  • Existing small business teaming network

How we will get to know each other

  1. Initial 30-minute fit conversation with the GovCon Division Lead
  2. Working session: walk through a real federal opportunity or account development scenario we are actively considering
  3. Reference checks (3+ professional references) and work history verification
  4. Engagement letter, scope of work, and rate confirmation
  5. Kickoff within 7 days of signed engagement

What we believe

Trust before revenue. Mission before money. Real seats, real upside. We build durable federal relationships through earned credibility. We win together. We pay people in real numbers, not pizza parties.

Application tips

  1. Visit , ,
  2. Find The Wilkinson Firm on LinkedIn
  3. In your cover note, answer two questions: (1) what kind of GovCon engagement shape works best for you (project-based, retained hours, hybrid), and (2) one example of a federal account or pursuit you would point to as your strongest reference work

What to expect from us

  • Reply within 48 hours
  • First-round conversation within 7 days of qualification
  • Full process: 2-4 weeks

jobs.excerpt: About NewWorldNewWorld is a media company that restores our ability to imagine a world better than the one we inherited.
jobs.description:
About NewWorld

NewWorld is a media company that restores our ability to imagine a world better than the one we inherited. We build the stories, worlds, and communities where that future stops feeling radical and starts feeling popular, possible, and ours to demand and get.

We do this three ways: original shows we own, strategy and Command Center services we deliver for clients, and shows with charitable purpose commissioned through our Media Fund. One studio, one method, one point of view.

What a Creative Command Center does

A Command Center is a small, senior, always-on team that connects four things normally kept apart: research (rigorous information on audiences and what/who they tune into), creators (the people our audiences usually trust more than other institutions), production (content shipped at the speed of the platforms), and amplification (taking the best and most responsive content and moving it creatively through the algorithm).

A Command Center works in two stages. The first is activation, which means identifying the voices a particular audience already trusts and briefing them well enough that they will speak in their own words about something they had not previously been talking about. Those voices are rarely the client's own channels and never paid spokespeople reading from a script. We are connecting to the credibility of creators, commentators, community figures and coalition partners who have standing we cannot manufacture ourselves.

The second stage is amplification, and it is where most creator programs fail. A creator post that reaches only its own following remains a piece of content, while the same post picked up by amplifier accounts, placed behind paid social and digital, pitched into earned media, extended into out-of-home or a live event, and coordinated with distribution partners becomes the conversation itself. Making that happen requires directing a bench of specialist vendors so that their work compounds rather than running in parallel lanes, which is a large part of this job.

The Command Center operates in both directions. Reactive work means breaking a false or predatory story before its frame hardens, on a timeline measured in hours rather than weeks. Proactive work means setting the terms of a conversation before anyone else has the chance to.

Earlier this year we built a Command Center for a candidate facing roughly $10 million in attack spending from pro-AI-industry groups, beginning from almost no name recognition. The work generated 22 million views in a district of 750,000 voters and more than a million engagements, outperforming the industry engagement benchmark by a factor of three and paid engagement by nearly twelve. He finished within four points of winning, and the attack that was meant to end his candidacy became the thing his campaign was best known for.

The role

You will run 1-2 Creative Command Centers. The work involves turning a narrative strategy into an operation that ships on a reliable cadence: setting the operating rhythm and the approval paths, writing and commissioning the briefs, building and managing the roster of trusted voices, and directing the vendors who amplify them so that paid media, creator management, earned media and production are all working from one calendar and one set of metrics. You will also be the senior NewWorld person in the room with the client, which means you are trusted to make decisions without checking first.

The Command Centers coming online over the next year sit in different worlds, including financial confidence, product launches, worker power, gender and identity, product marketing, climate resilience and electoral politics, and we are not looking for a subject-matter expert in any one of them. What we need is someone who has moved between worlds over the course of their own career and can become fluent in a new one quickly, because that adaptation is the job rather than a prelude to it.

Who we are looking for

We are looking for eight to twelve or more years of experience across some combination of creator and influencer strategy, integrated campaign leadership, digital media, cultural and narrative strategy, brand, entertainment production, or rapid response. The shape of the experience matters more to us than the number of years.

  • You have owned something end to end and been accountable for the outcome rather than only the deliverables.
  • You have built a channel or an audience from nothing, whether a YouTube channel, a TikTok account, a newsletter, a podcast, a show or a community. We weight this experience heavily, because it is the difference between commissioning content and understanding why content travels.
  • You have managed creators or talent directly, which means giving feedback that improves the work and holding a standard without flattening someone's voice.
  • You have run integrated campaigns across paid, earned and organic channels, and you have directed outside vendors rather than executing every channel yourself.
  • You write short-form copy exceptionally well. The brief is the product in this role, and a brief that is dense or unclear will not produce anything.
  • You have been the senior person on a client relationship, with the judgment to know when to push a recommendation and when to absorb a decision you disagree with.
  • You stay calm when a moment is live, and you are willing to be fierce without being cruel. We name the company and the decision rather than performing outrage for the algorithm.
  • Your career has moved across worlds in ways that might look scattered on a conventional resume and are precisely what this role requires.

What this role is not

This is a full-time position for someone who wants to build something over a period of years, not a contract or fractional engagement. It is not social media management, and it is not influencer marketing, since reach is the entry cost here rather than the outcome we are measured against. It is also not a role in which someone hands you a finished strategy to coordinate.

Compensation and benefits

The salary range is $130,000 to $165,000, set by experience, and candidates at the upper end of the experience range should expect an offer in the upper half of that band. The role includes full benefits, with health coverage, and paid time off. It is remote and US-based, with the option to work from our New York office.

Equal opportunity

Equity is at the heart of NewWorld. From the clients we partner with to the team we are building, we are committed to creating opportunities for the talented, creative professionals who have been systematically denied them across this industry. Women, people of color, LGBTI people, people of any religion or nationality, and people with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply.

How to apply

Send a resume along with a note of no more than 400 words responding to a single question: describe a moment when you needed to reach an audience that did not want to hear from you, and explain what you did. We would rather read one specific story than a cover letter.

Candidates who reach the shortlist will be asked to write a sample creator brief from a real prompt, and we pay for the time that takes.

Salary: $130,000 – $165,000

The Short Version: We aren’t building software to sell ads or optimize clicks. At Augintel, we build Natural Language Processing (NLP) software that helps social workers and clinicians read through mountains of messy case notes to find critical, life-saving information about kids and families.

Our tool can help a social worker understand a thousand-page case history in seconds. Because of our software, caseworkers are finding lost grandmothers so kids don't go to foster care, uncovering hidden risks, and quickly spotting if a child urgently needs diabetes medication.
We are a small, tight-knit team of five, and we need a Senior Software Engineer to help us build the infrastructure that makes this all possible.

What You Will Actually Do Here: We need you to build the heavy-lifting software around the AI. You will be working closely with a Machine Learning expert.

  • The Heavy Lifting (70%): The biggest chunk of your work will be building the engine that extracts insights from notes and indexes them for downstream consumers (APIs, our web app). This will entail designing and building pipelines that process millions of case notes reliably and at scale. This backend work is heavily driven by Python.
  • The Infrastructure: You will be configuring and using AWS (specifically ECS, OpenSearch, Lambda, and S3) and writing solid SQL (we use PostgreSQL).
  • The Web App (30%): The remaining portion of your work will involve the front-end user interface and APIs, where you will use TypeScript (React and NodeJS).

Who You Are:

  • You have 5+ years of real-world experience. We are looking for someone who is solidly mid-level (your second or third real job). You aren't an entry-level beginner, but you also aren't looking to be a hands-off architect or on a fast track to management. You just want to write great code and improve your craft.
  • You are independent. We are a remote team. We need someone who can work on their couch, figure things out, and know when to raise their hand for help without flailing.
  • You like talking to people. You will occasionally jump on video calls directly with our clients to troubleshoot issues, stand up new features, or whiteboard solutions. We don't want someone who just wants to sit in a dark closet and write code.
  • You want ownership. You won't just be blindly pulling widgets off a backlog. You will collaborate daily with our ML researcher, product manager, and clients to frame problems and design actual solutions.

The Perks:

  • 100% Remote (US-based). If you happen to be in the Chicago area, great—we have a local nexus here—but it is absolutely not required.
  • Get hands-on experience working right alongside cutting-edge Machine Learning and NLP technology.
  • Go to sleep every night knowing your code is actively keeping kids safe and giving social workers their time back.

If you are a solid Python, Typescript and AWS developer who wants to use your powers for good, we want to talk to you.

jobs.description:
Job Summary:

At the Center for Education Policy Research at Harvard University (CEPR) our mission is to transform education through the power of quality evidence. We believe that if we want to dramatically improve educational outcomes for all children, evidence must play a critical role.

The Math Teaching and Teacher Learning team at CEPR provides math-specific professional development to teachers and coaches to help improve math instruction. Our current grant-funded projects seek to develop and test an expanded math-specific coach training program (M-Powering Teacher Coaching) that uses machine-learning automated feedback and AI-enhanced coaching tools. The Data Scientist will contribute to this and other projects that connect rigorous educational research with practical tools for teachers, instructional coaches, and education leaders. This person will oversee, manage, and lead analysis and application of complex datasets, and contribute to the integration of research insights into innovative educational tools and cutting-edge products. They will be joining a team with faculty lead and Principal Investigator, Heather Hill, and collaborators at higher education research institutions, professional learning organizations, curriculum providers, and Enterprise AI firm(s).

Job-Specific Responsibilities:

Key responsibilities of the Data Scientist include:

Data and Research Infrastructure:

  • Organizes, cleans, and prepares structured and unstructured data (e.g., video, audio, text) for AI modeling and analysis.
  • Develops and documents codebooks, annotation protocols, data dictionaries, and other research procedures.
  • Builds and documents reproducible workflows for data processing, annotation, statistical analysis, and modeling.
  • Supports shared practices for version control, code review, data security, and reproducible research.
  • Maintains organized project files, code repositories, data documentation, and analytic records.

Analysis and Measurement Development

  • Conduct data science work across grant-funded projects focused on teaching, instructional coaching, curriculum, and artificial intelligence in education.
  • Applies statistical, machine learning, natural language processing, and generative AI methods as appropriate.
  • Coordinates and executes the development and evaluation of automated measures related to teaching, coaching, curriculum implementation, and teacher learning.
  • Supports pilot studies and evaluation activities related to usability, implementation, coaching, and teacher experience.

Product Development and Dissemination

  • Helps integrate research measures and findings into education tools and user interfaces.
  • Contributes to research papers, reports, public goods, funder deliverables, and other project materials (e.g., tables, figures, visualization, presentations, and technical documentation)

Project Management and Cross-team Collaboration

  • Manages timelines and deliverables across one or more grant-funded workstreams
  • Collaborates with researchers, educators, software developers, and external partners such as Enterprise AI firm(s) to support project goals.
  • Oversees internal working groups to deliver on tasks and milestones

Performs other duties as assigned.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, Mathematics, Education, Social Science, or a related field.
  • Relevant experience, which may include professional, research, internship, or concurrent-with-baccalaureate experience in data science, statistical programming, machine learning, educational research, or a related field.
  • Must have strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively.
  • Occasional travel may be required to support project meetings, trainings, pilot activities, or other research-related events.
  • Candidates should submit a resume or curriculum vitae and cover letter describing their relevant experience and interest in the position.
  • All candidates invited to the in-person/hybrid interview may be asked to complete a task and/or submit a sample program.

This is a full-time, one-year term appointment beginning on the date of hire, with the possibility of continuation based on funding, performance, and departmental needs.

The work arrangement is remote, subject to project and departmental needs.

Additional Qualifications and Skills:

  • Master’s degree in data science, statistics, computer science, education, economics, social science, or a related field preferred.
  • Experience with R, Python, Stata, or a similar programming language preferred.
  • Experience with machine learning, natural language processing, generative AI, or automated scoring strongly preferred.
  • Experience with data annotation, codebook development, or qualitative and quantitative coding preferred.
  • Familiarity with building reproducible workflows for data cleaning, processing, analysis, or modeling preferred.
  • Familiarity with version control, databases, APIs, or collaborative software development preferred.
  • Experience with K-12 education data or education research is a plus.
  • Experience with mathematics teaching and learning is a plus.
  • Interest in improving education through responsible and evidence-based uses of artificial intelligence; commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, and belonging.
  • Appointment End Date: One year from date of hire
  • Standard Hours/Schedule: 35 hours per week
  • Compensation Range/Rate (including Shift Differential if applicable): $90,000 - $95,000 commensurate with experience
  • Visa Sponsorship Information: Harvard University is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position
  • Pre-Employment Screening: Identity and Education

Work Format Details

This position has been determined by school or unit leaders that the duties and responsibilities can effectively be performed fully remotely at a non-Harvard location. Employees in fully remote positions must work all scheduled hours in a Harvard registered state in compliance with the University’s Policy on Employment Outside of Massachusetts. At the discretion of the department, fully remote employees may occasionally be required on site at a Harvard location. Certain visa types and funding sources may limit work location. By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.

Why join the Harvard Graduate School of Education?

The Harvard Graduate School of Education (HGSE) is a diverse community of learners, teachers, and employees who are passionate about changing the world through education and striving for maximum impact in the field of education.

TWF has built the scaffolding for federal work. MBE certification, SAM.gov registration, two operational divisions ready to serve federal contracts, a credentialed bench, and signed commercial customers proving the operating model. What is missing is the capture function. This engagement is for the operator who knows how to walk a federal opportunity from first signal through awarded contract, and who wants to build that function inside a firm where it does not exist yet.

What is already built

The Wilkinson Firm is a workforce strategy and staffing firm headquartered across NC and Atlanta. We launched in April 2025 and are now in Year 2 of operations. Two operational divisions today (HR Advisory for the mental health industry, Premium Hospitality and Event Staffing). Government Contracting division being formally stood up this quarter. Hourly consulting rate, three tiers calibrated to experience and scope:

  • Director ($200-350/hr): Established capture directors with documented win history on $1M+ contracts

Engagement is hourly. Time commitment scales with pipeline activity, typically 10-40 hours per week. Win-based bonus stack negotiable on top of hourly rate for awarded contracts the engagement materially drove.

  • Day 180: 2-4 proposals submitted. First award or shortlist position. Win rate baseline established.

Who you are

  • Shipley-trained or equivalent. SAM.gov fluent. Comfortable with FAR/DFARS terminology

  3. Reference checks (3+ professional references) and work history verification

2-4 weeks first conversation to active engagement.

What we believe

Trust before revenue. Mission before money. Real seats, real upside. We build durable federal relationships through earned credibility. We win together. We pay people in real numbers, not pizza parties. We are building something great and we want partners who feel the same.

jobs.description:
Hello, our name is Customertimes, but you can call us CT. We are a global digital engineering, product development, and technology consulting company. Headquartered in New York, we have a team of 1000+ experts working across 65+ countries.

About this job:

We're looking for an experienced Senior Project Manager to lead the delivery of a large-scale enterprise data platform built on Databricks.

This is a client-facing role where you'll take ownership of delivery across planning, execution, quality, budget, and stakeholder management. You'll work closely with architects, engineering teams, business analysts, and senior client stakeholders to ensure the platform continues to deliver reliable business value while supporting future growth.

The platform is already in production and supports business reporting, analytics, and planning across multiple business domains. As the platform evolves, the focus is on improving scalability, optimizing platform costs, strengthening data quality, and delivering new capabilities through a well-defined roadmap.

Location: Europe

How you'll make an impact:

  • Own end-to-end delivery of the enterprise data platform, including scope, planning, budget, timelines, quality, and client communication;
  • Drive delivery across distributed Data Engineering, BI, and Business Analysis teams;
  • Collaborate with engineering and architecture leads to improve platform efficiency and optimize consumption-based infrastructure costs;
  • Ensure strong delivery governance, including backlog management, change control, Definition of Ready, Definition of Done, and clear documentation of requirements;
  • Work closely with client architects and technical stakeholders to review solution designs, discuss architectural decisions, and resolve complex delivery challenges;
  • Support high standards of data quality, reconciliation, and reliability across multiple data sources;
  • Manage delivery risks, dependencies, and priorities while maintaining transparency with stakeholders;
  • Own roadmap planning and execution, ensuring predictable and successful delivery of platform enhancements;
  • Build trusted relationships with client stakeholders and contribute to the long-term growth of the engagement.

Within the first several months, you will:

  • Help improve platform stability and data reliability;
  • Establish predictable delivery processes and transparent project governance;
  • Improve visibility into platform costs and help the client understand cost drivers;
  • Strengthen collaboration with client architecture and business teams;
  • Deliver roadmap milestones on schedule while maintaining high quality standards.

What makes you a great fit:

  • 10+ years of experience in Delivery or Project Management, including ownership of large-scale BI, Data Platform, or Data Engineering programs;
  • Proven experience managing end-to-end project delivery, including scope, budget, timelines, quality, and stakeholder management;
  • Experience delivering enterprise data platforms built on Databricks or similar technologies such as Snowflake or Google BigQuery;
  • Good understanding of modern data engineering concepts, including ETL/ELT pipelines, incremental loading, semantic or dimensional data modeling, data quality, and lineage;
  • Experience working with cloud-based data platforms and orchestration tools such as Airflow, dbt, or similar;
  • Strong client-facing communication and stakeholder management skills, with experience working directly with senior business and technical leaders;
  • Experience working within Agile delivery environments using Jira or similar project management tools;
  • Ability to coordinate cross-functional distributed teams across Engineering, Business Analysis, and BI;
  • English level: C1 or higher, with confidence communicating directly with international clients and leading meetings.

You are a star if you have:

  • Experience in Consumer Goods, Manufacturing, Retail, Healthcare, or other data-intensive industries;
  • Familiarity with Salesforce, SAP, Microsoft ecosystem, or Power BI;
  • Previous experience working within Databricks or SAP partner ecosystems;
  • Experience delivering semantic data models or AI-ready data platforms;
  • Exposure to AI, forecasting, anomaly detection, or analytical use cases built on enterprise data platforms;
  • Experience working alongside multiple vendors in complex enterprise environments.

Technology landscape:

The platform is built primarily on Databricks, with modern cloud infrastructure and orchestration tooling. Data is integrated from systems such as Salesforce, SAP, and Microsoft solutions, with Power BI used for reporting and analytics. The platform also includes a semantic layer designed to support future AI and advanced analytics initiatives.

If you're looking to contribute to global projects, grow your skills, shape the way you work, and be part of a connected international community — Customertimes is the place to build your next career chapter. Are you ready to spark the tech with us?

Nous sommes à la recherche d’une personne pour occuper le poste de directeur du développement des affaires au sein du SIAI, afin de stimuler la croissance, la fidélisation et l’expansion des solutions offertes par le SIAI et du service MPRI partout au Canada. La personne retenue aura un rôle de « conseiller/conseillère de confiance » auprès des clients municipaux et du secteur de l’assurance, tout en collaborant avec les experts internes afin de soutenir l’intégration des clients, la mise en œuvre des solutions et leur réussite à long terme.

Job Description: Chief KYC (Know Your Customer) Officer (CKYCO)

Industry: Banking, Financial Services, Insurance, Investment

Job Type: Full-Time

Reporting To: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) / Chief AML Officer (CAMLO) / Chief Risk Officer (CRO)

Job Summary

The Chief KYC Officer (CKYCO) is responsible for overseeing the organization's KYC, Customer Due Diligence (CDD), and onboarding frameworks to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and effective management of customer-related risks.

This role plays a critical part in preventing financial crime by ensuring robust customer identification, verification, and risk assessment processes across all business lines.

Key Responsibilities

1. KYC Strategy & Framework

Develop and implement enterprise-wide KYC/CDD strategies and frameworks

Ensure alignment with AML/CFT regulations and organizational policies

Establish risk-based customer onboarding and due diligence processes

Continuously enhance KYC practices to address emerging risks

2. Customer Due Diligence (CDD/EDD)

Oversee CDD and Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) processes

Ensure accurate customer identification, verification, and risk profiling

Manage onboarding of high-risk customers and complex cases

Ensure compliance with regulatory KYC requirements

3. KYC Operations & Process Management

Oversee end-to-end KYC operations, including onboarding, periodic reviews, and remediation

Improve operational efficiency and turnaround time for KYC processes

Standardize KYC procedures across business units

Monitor and resolve KYC backlogs and issues

4. Regulatory Compliance & Reporting

Ensure compliance with KYC-related regulatory requirements

Support AML and compliance teams in regulatory reporting and audits

Maintain audit-ready documentation and records

Monitor regulatory changes impacting KYC processes

5. Risk Assessment & Monitoring

Conduct customer risk assessments and segmentation

Monitor high-risk customers, PEPs, and complex client structures

Identify and mitigate customer-related risks

Align KYC practices with enterprise risk frameworks

6. Technology & KYC Automation

Oversee KYC systems, tools, and digital onboarding platforms

Drive automation and digital transformation in KYC processes

Implement data analytics and AI tools for customer risk assessment

Ensure integration with AML and transaction monitoring systems

7. Stakeholder Collaboration

Collaborate with AML, compliance, risk, and business teams

Support front-line teams in customer onboarding and due diligence

Liaise with regulators, auditors, and external stakeholders

Provide KYC insights and reporting to leadership

8. Leadership & Team Management

Lead and develop KYC operations and compliance teams

Establish performance standards and KPIs

Foster a culture of compliance, accuracy, and efficiency

Support talent development and succession planning

Key Requirements

Education

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Finance, Business Administration, Law, or related field

Professional certifications such as CAMS, ICA, or equivalent are highly preferred

Experience

10–15+ years of experience in KYC, AML, compliance, or financial crime roles

Proven experience in senior KYC leadership roles (e.g., Head of KYC, KYC Director)

Strong experience in banking, financial services, insurance, or investment sectors

Skills & Competencies

Deep knowledge of KYC/CDD/EDD processes and AML regulations

Strong understanding of customer risk profiling and onboarding frameworks

Expertise in KYC operations and process optimization

Analytical and problem-solving skills

Leadership and team management

Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement

Attention to detail and compliance mindset

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

KYC onboarding turnaround time

Accuracy and completeness of customer records

Reduction in KYC backlogs and remediation cases

Compliance with regulatory requirements

Audit and regulatory inspection outcomes

Customer onboarding experience and satisfaction

Preferred Attributes

Experience in multinational or highly regulated financial institutions

Exposure to digital KYC, eKYC, and regtech solutions

Strong collaboration with AML, compliance, and risk teams

Ability to manage high-volume KYC operations

Compensation & Benefits

Competitive executive salary

Performance-based incentives

Executive benefits and allowances

The IT Manager - Enterprise Systems is a key role responsible for managing our integration and application development teams. The primary focus is to manage and coordinate Finance and Accounting, Merchandising, and Product Development application configuration, development and support (ERP, Toolio, Centric, and related systems), application extension development, application and data integration, and analytics development. This role will act as a strategic partner to business leaders, with the ability to translate complex financial and merchandising requirements into technical roadmap specifications. Manages the implementations of key systems and reports on progress and adjustments to Technology leadership. This person will collaborate with IT leadership and provide input into the technology roadmap for Duluth Trading Company, ensuring solutions meet strategic and delivery expectations.

Position Details

Work Environment:

We are headquartered in the Madison, WI area, but this position is eligible for remote work within the continental United States, excluding California. Candidates must reside in and be legally authorized to work from an approved state. If you happen to live near and enjoy coming into the office, we will welcome you!

What You’ll Do:

  • Contribute to the design/roadmap, acquisition, management, and implementation of applications/systems and infrastructure
  • Be part of the Duluth IT leadership team that drives solution delivery to support Duluth business
  • Ensure development team is meeting delivery expectations and following industry leading architecture principles
  • Lead a team of product owners, application analysts and engineers, data integration, analytics, and system extension developers
  • Partner with other IT leaders to advance overall IT maturity and best practice adoption
  • Collaborate with business and IT stakeholders to shape vision and craft the roadmap for a specific product within DTC’s technology stack
  • Own, groom and facilitate refinement of the product backlog, using customer and business value to prioritize features
  • Collaborate with business stakeholders to define the business case for suggested enhancements and incorporate into scoping and prioritization
  • Define epics and user stories for the product backlog
  • Support technical and architectural roadmaps for the Finance and Accounting, Merchandising, and Product Development portfolios
  • Provide recommendations impacting the selection and use of information technology (e.g. platform, build/buy, integration, architecture specification)
  • Evaluate and analyze solutions from such perspectives as architecture, feasibility, and cost
  • Develop and mentor the team
  • Support the integrated technology roadmap aligned with business capabilities
  • Continuously evaluate and harness forward-looking design and development tools to position technology as a strategic asset and a key enabler for Duluth Trading Company
  • Identify and promote best practices, staying current on technological advances and making recommendations for tool/system usage to drive organizational growth & innovation and to maximize technology investment

What We’re Looking For:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, IT, or related field - Equivalent work experience will be considered
  • 7+ Years of experience
  • Experience in a retail environment, including ERP, Merchandising and Product Development domains
  • Software application development experience with ability to provide mobile app development input
  • Experience implementing governance, SLAs and best practices in an enterprise systems environment
  • Extensive experience in delivering a services/API first strategy and implementing unified services/API platforms in the cloud
  • Experience with Agile processes and supporting tooling
  • The ability to lead a team through the high-pressure environment of "Peak Season" (e.g., Black Friday/Cyber Monday) where system stability is paramount
  • Hands-on experience leading design, development, and implementation of solutions in a retail environment
  • Experience leading, configuring, or heavily contributing to major ERP implementations, upgrades, or significant enhancements (e.g., SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics 365)
  • Extensive experience with EDI, API integrations, and middleware that connect ERP systems to e-commerce platforms (e.g., Shopify, Salesforce Commerce Cloud), omnichannel and point-of-sale systems (e.g., Manhattan Active Omni) warehouse management systems (e.g., Manhattan Active WM)
  • Deep, foundational knowledge of core finance and accounting business processes, including General Ledger (GL), Accounts Payable (AP), Accounts Receivable (AR), fixed assets, and financial close processes
  • Direct experience configuring and troubleshooting complex revenue recognition rules unique to multi-channel environments (e.g., handling retail returns, wholesale chargebacks, deferred revenue for e-commerce gift cards).
  • Experience delivering technology solutions for multi-currency consolidation, automated bank reconciliations, tax compliance (e.g., Avalara, Vertex), and internal financial auditing.
  • Deep technical knowledge across IT domains: security, infrastructure, cloud, integration, database, analytics
  • Analytical, logical, and innovative
  • Understanding of existing enterprise and emerging systems
  • Strong business acumen to provide knowledge and counsel to internal IT and potential external collaboration partners
  • Excellent communication, presentation, influencing and reasoning skills
  • Authorization to work in the United States without sponsorship

Leadership Competencies:

Leading Self:

Leading Others:

  • Inspiring Trust
  • Adaptability
  • Mature Confidence
  • Career and Self Development
  • Driving Execution
  • Building Organizational Relationships
  • Empowering Others
  • Fostering Open Dialogue
  • Attracting & Developing Talent
  • Leadership Versatility

Physical Environment & Travel Expectations:

  • Travel is required for less than 10% of company-related meetings, programs, and/or events.
  • Sitting is required for 90% of working hours.
  • Standing is required for 10% of working hours.
  • Continuous arm, hand, and wrist movement (ie: typing)
  • Occasional reaching, twisting, and bending.
  • Noise level no greater than casual conversation.
  • Ability to perform work in cubicle workstations or an office setting.
  • Work in temperatures ranging from 65 - 75 degrees.

Onsite Interview & Onboarding Requirements:

To foster our collaborative culture, Duluth Trading Company incorporates in-person touch points into our hiring and onboarding experience for this remote role:

  • Final Interview: Held on-site at our office in Mount Horeb, WI, giving you a firsthand look at our workspace and daily operations.

  • HQ Onboarding: Newly hired team members will spend their first week of onboarding live at our headquarters to kickstart training and team integration.

✈️ Travel Note: Duluth Trading Company will fully coordinate and fund all travel arrangements and accommodations for both the final interview and the onboarding week.

Duluth Headquarters Benefits and Perks

Our pursuit of a better way isn't just about our products—it's about our people too. That's why our Dam Good Crew enjoys a comprehensive benefits package, designed to support their well-being and success.

  • Multiple Medical plan options

Position Compensation Outline

Compensation Range: $115,000 - $130,000/year

About Duluth Trading Company

Started in 1989, Duluth Trading Company exists to enable hard-working individuals to take on life with their own two hands. Folks that revel in doing it the hard way and celebrate finding a better way. We seek talented individuals who share these beliefs and are excited to further the Duluth Trading legacy with a digital-first mindset, always moving forward and always innovating.

From ingenious Duluth workwear, to comfortably capable Buck Naked Underwear, to outside-embracing AKHG, it’s all about the innovative gear and gadgets that equip customers for a more hands-on way of life.
